rows.notes: The study is a perspective/opinion letter that develops a conceptual framework (six hypotheses on zombie ideas adapted from Quiggin, Krugman, Peters and Nagel) and argues that modern irrigation technologies aggravate water scarcity. It reports no original data, experiment, survey or model runs; its only quantitative material (figure 2: 230 case studies, 70.4% reduced availability elsewhere, etc.) is reproduced from the authors' earlier review (P<U+00E9>rez-Blanco et al 2020). The claim that altered return flows reduce water availability for other uses and complicate governance is asserted in Section 2 and Section 3.3 by argument and citation of other work, not as an own result. Q1 is therefore 'no' and all other questions 'no'.

notes: Document is complete (letter plus references). It is a non-empirical perspective piece; supplementary methods on the zombie-idea framework are not included in the text.
